reason: Selected recovery ablations support retaining failure knowledge while restoring executable state.

candidates.title: Retain failure lessons when restoring a prior agent state
candidates.rule: For reversible long-horizon tasks, compare rollback with persistent structured reflection against rollback-only and reflection-only recovery.
candidates.passage: neither component alone matches the complete method
candidates.finding: On ScienceWorld with DeepSeek-V3, combined recovery reaches 76.75% success versus 70.48% for reflection-only and 69.37% for rollback-only. The broader method is strongest in eight of nine model-benchmark settings; Reflexion leads the remaining GAIA cell.
candidates.conditions: All recovery components use the acting backbone. The same task interface and interaction budgets apply; GAIA workspace files are restored along with the trajectory.
candidates.limitations: State restoration must be feasible and complete; these results do not authorize undoing irreversible external actions. Interaction-budget matching is not necessarily total compute matching. The formal optimal-policy inclusion result is not a guarantee of realized improvement.
candidates.validation_test: Compare full, reflection-only and rollback-only recovery at measured total cost. Check restored files and environment state, recurrence of the same error, final success and regressions.

review_scope: Selected abstract, introduction, methods or main-result sections; not a comprehensive paper or appendix review.
